notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose my major because ever since I was a little kid, I always knew I wanted to go into a profession where I could help others. At different points in my life, I wanted to be a teacher, a psychologist, and eventually a doctor. Whenever a friend or family member was sick or hurt, I found myself wanting to be there for them, whether that meant helping with an injury, checking on them, or simply making sure they felt cared for. I have always found a lot of meaning in being someone others can rely on. When I first applied to college, I was unsure of exactly what I wanted to do, so I explored psychology. Although I enjoyed learning about people and understanding why we think and behave the way we do, I still felt like something was missing. I kept coming back to my interest in medicine and the direct impact healthcare professionals can have on someone's life. That feeling led me toward my current major and my interest in pursuing a career as a Physician Assistant. What excites me most about healthcare is the combination of science and human connection. I want a career where I can continue learning while also building relationships with the people I am helping. I know I still have a lot to learn about the different paths within healthcare, and I am excited to explore them. Ultimately, I want to enter a field where I can make people feel heard, supported, and cared for during some of the most hardest moments of their lives.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED

While I am currently very interested in becoming a Physician Assistant, I know that there is still so much about the healthcare field that I have yet to experience and learn about. I hope to make meaningful relationships and connections through this fraternity. I think having people around me who share similar goals and interests will help motivate me throughout college and as I work toward my career. I would love the opportunity to learn from other members about their experiences, get advice about preparing for a career in healthcare, and eventually being able to provide that same support to newer members. I also want to take advantage of the volunteer opportunities that MED provides so I can gain more hands-on exposure to some different areas of the medical field while helping the community. I am excited to learn from guest speakers and hear about their experiences and career paths, and hopefully be able to shadow a few of them. I am excited about possibly utilizing the resources and connections MED can provide by meeting healthcare professionals and other students who can help me learn more about the field. I think these experiences and connections would help me explore my interests and better understand what I want my future in healthcare to look like.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My experiences working and volunteering have helped me develop skills that I know will be important in a career in healthcare. One of the most meaningful experiences I have had was volunteering at Cleveland Clinic. I helped stock inpatient rooms and assisted nurses with different tasks, but one of my favorite parts was being able to interact with patients. Even though some of my responsibilities were small, being around patients and seeing how nurses cared for them gave me a better understanding of how important compassion, communication, and patience are in healthcare. It also made me more excited about wanting to work in a field where I can directly help people. Working at Hollister and HomeGoods has also taught me a lot about interacting with people. I have had to learn how to communicate with all different types of customers, work with my coworkers, and stay calm when things get busy. Sometimes it’s as simple as listening to someone and figuring out what they need but I have learned that those small interactions can make a difference in someone's experience. I think that will carry over into healthcare because being able to talk to patients and make them feel comfortable is something I really value. I also volunteered at a church a few days before Thanksgiving to help give out canned and boxed meals to families in the community. I liked being able to see the people we were helping and knowing that the time we spent preparing and handing out meals was going directly toward helping families during the holidays. It made volunteering feel less like something I was doing for the hours and more like something I genuinely enjoyed doing. Overall, these experiences have given me different opportunities to work with and care for people. My experience at the Cleveland Clinic especially helped me realize that I want a career where I can have that kind of interaction with patients every day. I know healthcare will come with challenges, but these experiences have made me excited to pursue medicine and help others every day.

I haven't worked a large variety of jobs throughout my lifetime, but the ones I have worked have certainly prepared me for a career in healthcare. I was a shift lead at my local juice shop for several years, and I learned how to communicate and lead effectively. These skills are vital in healthcare, especially as an aspiring vet. Through my shadowing opportunities, I've seen how the veterinarian has to communicate with the vet techs and assistants to ensure a surgery goes smoothly. Additionally, the customer service I learned is important for relating to clients. Explaining details such as prices and health benefits parallels vet med because I can better explain how much a medicine or procedure will cost and how it will help their animal. Additionally, lifeguarding has taught me the importance of teamwork and quick response. In training, we practice saves where all of us lifeguards have to work together to save a victim. For example, someone is responsible for the AED, someone is responsible for compressions, someone is responsible for oxygen, and someone is responsible for the crowd. This life-saving teamwork is very similar to the setup I have seen at veterinary practices. Each person has a job and communicates with each other under high-stakes circumstances. These skills are necessary for a career in healthcare. Also, running cross country and track competitively in high school taught me how to excel under pressure. My team won multiple state championships, and being a top runner on a state-contending team taught me how to control adrenaline and stay focused. Harnessing adrenaline is an essential skill for the life-saving responsibilities associated with healthcare.
All of these skills, in addition to my shelter volunteering and shadowing experience, have made me significantly more prepared for a healthcare career than I ever thought I would be.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: The two biggest things for me when it comes to joining MED are community and resources. All of my friends are business and criminal justice majors, so studying with people and talking about career paths really never came up. When I ran into Stefani while studying for our Bio 2 final, I learned about the fraternity and started to like the idea of being able to study and talk with others in my field more often. You guys seem like a super cool group of people with a lot in common, and I would love to be a part of that circle. I am also really interested in all of the resources the fraternity has to offer. The biggest one is research opportunities, which I have desperately been trying to be a part of since attending the University of Tampa. Being able to have exclusive opportunities to be a part of those labs is a dream come true, and one of the biggest unchecked boxes on my undergrad wishlist. I'm currently volunteering in one now as a test subject, with hopes that the professor likes me enough to bring me on to her team. I also really like the volunteer opportunities you offer. As someone going into healthcare, my biggest concern is helping people. For example, I love giving to the homeless in the city with my extra swipes, and doing the volunteer work offered through you guys would be another great way to give back to the community. I always want to do volunteer work, but I can never seem to find any openings.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I have a couple of good traits, such as social skills, study habits, and networking. Firstly, I believe my personality would fit right in with the brothers. I tend to get along with everyone in my science classes, and I would assume the same when it comes to most members of the fraternity. I also enjoy studying with partners or groups. With that, I would love to get into study groups with like-minded people in the same classes as me and offer help + discuss the material so we can all get a better understanding. Another thing I do really well is networking. I've done a great job so far of building my network of professors and professionals, and I believe that, with the support and resources of MED, I would be able to continue to do so, weaving those into the fraternity and creating more opportunities throughout the frat for current and future members.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: With shadowing experiences in various work environments such as Physical Therapy, Physician, and Physician Assistant, I have started to grasp a solid foundation of how the healthcare field works. They keep things very organized and professional and also tend to know their stuff very well. These experiences enlightened me to take my undergraduate studies as seriously as possible, making sure to drill all of the material into my brain to ensure a seamless transition into the profession. But I've done a lot more than shadow and assist healthcare professionals. I would first like to talk about my experience as a soccer referee. When refereeing children's soccer, it's very important to stand strong in high-speed and high-stress environments. People running and screaming when calls are made is normal, and your job as a referee is to stay calm during these experiences and deliver appropriate responses to every situation. I also managed a boba stand at a very popular asian festival located here in Tampa. The festival was 3 days long, with 12-hour shifts that gave no breaks. Aside from all of the duties of a normal worker, I was also tasked with implementing systems to ensure a smooth run throughout these busy days. Doing things like maximizing efficiency when it came to making drinks, creating an organized ordering system, and handling specific customer requests all came with the job as the manager. I learned leadership and problem-solving over those 3 days, which are very applicable to the healthcare field. Additionally, I do babysitting for a family back home. Watching these kids through the years has taught me how to take care of people, listen, respond in appropriate ways to ensure compliance, and bond with them. If you're working with someone for long periods of time, the process is much more enjoyable when you grow a connection with them, as I've learned through babysitting. All of these lessons were extremely important and will be applied to how I operate in the medical field.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
Growing up, I always knew that I wanted to become a doctor. I think it was watching Grey's Anatomy. However, it wasn't until my sophomore year of high school that my true passion for healthcare took flight. I got my first job as a cashier at a local pharmacy. I became fascinated by how medications could interact with the body and treat illnesses. I found myself curious about how all the different drugs work and wanting to learn more.

My interest grew even further when I earned my pharmacy technician license and was allowed to be able to fill prescriptions. Being able to take on that responsibility gave me a small idea about what it would be like to be a pharmacist, and I was immediately hooked. I realized that pharmacy is something I could do for the rest of my life, and with my combined interest in healthcare, I knew that being a pharmacist was what I wanted.

What I'm most passionate about in healthcare is how the pharmacy field is constantly changing. It fascinates me how bacteria/disease can develop resistance to our medications, but then scientists develop new drugs. I love the idea of always being able to learn something new and the fact that, unfortunately, there will be someone who needs help. However, I want to be able to figure out if there is something out there that can help them. I'm good at problem-solving and connecting to people. I know deep down this career is for me.

notes.text:
My clinical and leadership experiences have prepared me for the responsibilities of a career in healthcare by exposing me to different environments, allowing me to build a well-rounded mindset and leadership abilities. 

Serving as President of my school’s Pre-Med Program, I had the opportunity to participate in clinical training at FAU Medical School, make rounds at West Boca Medical Center, and hear from healthcare professionals across various specialties, providing me with hands on experiences. I also took part in a four-year internship at the Dermatology Center of Wellington, which taught me essential bedside manner and the basics of Dermatology.

Additionally, founding a skincare blog for teens allowed me to help give back to my community by sharing accessible health information.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: The most impactful experience that I have had that has better prepared me for a career in healthcare was this past summer shadowing at an immediate care facility under a physician assistant. This was my first real exposure into my aspiring career as a PA. I spent the majority of my time shadowing observing patient interactions, each with a different set of circumstances, which was an eye-opening experience that showed me the gentle care, professionalism, and knowledge that is required to provide patients with the utmost level of care. When I was not observing patient interactions, I spent my time talking to and gaining insight from faculty members including APRN's, Physicians, and other PA's. Also, I took notes on every new piece of information and terminology that I encountered so that I could begin building the foundation that will support me as I progress through both the academic and clinical process of the pre-PA track. In addition to this experience, I have been a retail sales associate at various running specialty stores for over four years. This job mostly includes providing customers with the proper running shoes by walking them though a detailed fitting process that includes both a static and dynamic gait analysis. I look at pressure scans, foot measurements, weight bearing, and movement patterns to fit a customer into the proper shoe so that they can continue along their running and fitness journey successfully. I find it extremely important to explain to each customer my observations as well as the footwear selections I made based on their foot scan and gait analysis. As a result, customers can walk away feeling confident in their decision and motivated to continue running. I feel both of these experiences have and will continue to prepare me for taking on greater responsibilities in a healthcare setting because I am improving my ability to interact with patients, beginning to develop my practical skills in a healthcare setting, and setting the highest possible standard for the level of care that I will strive to provide patients with when I have the responsibilities that come with a career in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose biology on the pre med track because when I imagine my future, the idea of helping people brings out a passion in me that nothing else ever has. During my sophomore year of high school, I was able to experience firsthand how impactful kind surgeons and nurses can be on someone’s life. I was able to see the field of healthcare as a patient. I had developed a severe sinus infection that spread through my skull to my brain. I was left hospitalized for a week. I remember feeling so comfortable when a doctor would take time to really explain things to me. I was also able to feel the anxiety of feeling rushed or unseen by certain doctors. I’ll never forget watching young kids push IV stands up and down the hallways. Seeing children go through things so much more difficult than I was crushed me. Ever since my experience, the idea of being able to bring light into kids lives while also improving their health means everything. I want to be the doctor that takes time with his patients instead of herding them through the hospital. I have fallen in love with serving people in need of help. I find more fulfillment in that than I ever have doing anything else. I am also a christian and believe that this is the path God has for me. I don’t think many other careers could bring me the level of fulfillment the medical field will.

I see MED as helping hand and a way to hangout with good people in the process. I am also very exited at the possibility of getting more involved around Tampa. I love getting involved in things and have always been someone to take action instead of sitting back and waiting for an oppurtunity to come my way. notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: The jobs and experiences I have had have taught me skills I believe will be very beneficial to my future career in healthcare. One of my biggest learning experiences was running my own car detailing company in high school. I learned how to communicate with customers, problem solve, and work alongside my co-founder. It was the first thing in my life I had complete and total responsibility for. It taught me how to take ownership of my action and that the world wasn’t as black and white as school made it seem. In school failing a test could mean the end of someones grade and is very looked down upon. However, when I ran my own buisness, most of my learning came through trial and error. It gave me a healthy relationship with failure and showed me that the world doesn’t end when I fail. I know medicine requires extremely high standards but I also know that being a great student and future physician requires constantly learning, accepting feedback, and growing from setbacks. Another oppurtunity I had was to shadow Dr. Nuckols (Ear, Nose Throat surgeon) for a week. I was able to observe Dr. Nuckols interact with patients and also perform surgeries. This experience inside the operating room helped me center my goals on surgery. I was able to watch Nuckols and his team work together in an organized fashion. It taught me so much about teamwork. Everyone in the operating room had a job and relied on eachother to complete them. This showed me just how much you have to trust and maintain healthy relationship with you co-workers. The way Nuckols spoke to his patients pre and post operation also stuck out to me. He sympathized with there worries and made there questions feel heard while also bring a strong sense of confidence. He was able to walk them through there worries and the procedures in a way that made them feel safe. He showed me how important it is to display peaceful body language and manner. I know the responsibilities I will face in healthcare will be much greater, but I believe these experiences have given me a strong foundation to continue building on.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: Throughout high school and into college, my extracurriculars and jobs have given me a very realistic understanding of the responsibility that comes with healthcare. It isn't just about learning biology or doing well on exams; it’s about learning how to be accountable, stay calm under pressure, and take care of people when they are vulnerable.Through the medical magnet program at my high school, I was able to get hands-on experience that most students don't get until much later. During ambulance ride-alongs with EMTs, I saw firsthand how fast pre-hospital emergencies move. The paramedics trusted me to place 12-lead EKGs and check vitals, which taught me how to keep a steady hand and focus on the patient even when a situation feels intense. In the hospital, getting to shadow different departments and stand in an operating room to observe a live surgery showed me how much discipline and teamwork go into patient care, especially when it comes to keeping sterile fields and communicating clearly.Outside the clinical setting, volunteering and working at blood drives for all four years of high school taught me how to provide comfort to patients. Whenever someone felt faint or dizzy after donating, it was up to me to monitor them, get them juice and snacks, and make sure they felt safe. That taught me attentiveness and how important it is to notice the small details in how someone is doing.Even competing in parliamentary procedure through HOSA and working customer service jobs at Just Salad and Little Caesars helped prepare me. HOSA taught me how to speak up under time pressure and work through formal decisions with a team, while food service taught me work ethic, multitasking, and keeping a positive attitude during busy rushes. All of these experiences have helped shape my discipline, time management, and passion for medicine as I continue on the pre-health track

Through many labs and hands-on work, I found my love and passion for studying life itself.  Throughout the duration of junior year AP Biology, I was set on becoming a doctor. I wanted to help cure sick people and believed becoming a doctor was going to be my way to help. However, towards the end of my junior year, a program I was a part of required all students to shadow a healthcare worker I chose to shadow a very close friend’s mom who was the director of the endodontics program. After shadowing that day, a spark lit inside of me. Watching the resident work on one specific area and master the technique of performing a root canal, I was hooked. After that day, I immediately knew dentistry was something I would be passionate about and wanted to make it my career.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose biology pre-med out of a passion for science. I have always been fascinated with understanding the "why" behind things, and being able to break down the complex components of the human body. During my experience with clinical shadowing in high school, my favorite healthcare workers took the time to explain the chemistry behind the treatment plan they were choosing. I found myself drawn not only to the science itself, but also to the way that scientific knowledge could be applied to directly improve a patient's health. That experience helped me realize that healthcare combines many of the things I value most: curiosity, problem-solving, continuous learning, and meaningful connections with others. I enjoy learning how different systems of the body interact and how small changes at the cellular or molecular level can have significant effects on a person’s overall health. At the same time, I want my education to have a purpose beyond understanding science in a classroom. I want to use that knowledge to help people make informed decisions about their health and feel supported throughout their care. My interest in healthcare has also grown from seeing how much trust patients place in their healthcare providers. A strong healthcare professional must be knowledgeable and analytical, but also compassionate, communicative, and willing to listen. I want to develop those qualities throughout my education and eventually become someone who can make patients feel understood while providing thoughtful, evidence-based care. Ultimately, I chose biology pre-med because it gives me the foundation to explore my passion for science while preparing me for a career where that knowledge can make a tangible difference in people’s lives. Healthcare is where I see my curiosity and desire to help others coming together.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED

Medical school can be challenging, and I believe having a supportive group of peers who understand the journey is invaluable. I hope to build meaningful relationships with study buddies and friends who can motivate me to keep going, especially during difficult moments. I also hope to find opportunities to serve my community and make a meaningful impact outside of the classroom. Through service, I want to better understand the needs of those around me and grow into a physician who leads with compassion and purpose. Additionally, I am excited about the possibility of finding common ground with other members through shared interests, experiences, and goals. I hope these connections will create an environment where we can learn from one another and encourage each other to grow. Finally, I hope MED will introduce me to research opportunities and mentors who can help me explore my academic interests. Overall, I want MED to be a source of connection, growth, and motivation, a community that challenges me to become a better student, researcher, future physician, and person while reminding me that I do not have to navigate this journey alone.

notes.text: I believe I would contribute to MED through my passion for science, commitment to academic excellence, and desire to build meaningful connections with others. Maintaining a 4.0 GPA has taught me the importance of discipline, consistency, and hard work, but my academic interests extend beyond simply earning good grades. I am genuinely curious about science and especially enjoy opportunities to understand concepts deeply and share that knowledge with others. As a chemistry lab mentor, I have developed my ability to communicate complex ideas clearly, work collaboratively, and support students who may be struggling or lacking confidence. I would also contribute a strong interpersonal side to MED. Becoming more social and personable has been an intentional part of my personal growth, and I have learned how much I enjoy making others feel comfortable and included. My clinical experiences reinforced this for me. I especially enjoyed working with elderly patients and others who may experience loneliness or need additional social support. I found that sometimes simply taking the time to listen, talk, or make someone feel seen can be just as meaningful as providing practical assistance. I hope to bring that same compassion and willingness to connect to MED. Additionally, I am very interested in research and would be excited to engage with MED beyond regular meetings. I would especially value attending events where I could meet researchers, learn about their work, and potentially find opportunities to become involved in research myself. I am eager to learn from others, build relationships, and contribute wherever I can. Overall, I would bring curiosity, reliability, compassion, and enthusiasm to MED, along with a genuine desire to learn, connect with others, and contribute to the community.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My experiences in clinical, volunteer, and campus settings have shown me that a career in healthcare requires much more than an understanding of science. It requires patience, empathy, communication, adaptability, and a genuine willingness to serve others. Through clinical experiences in an assisted living facility, emergency room, and physical therapy setting, I have had the opportunity to observe patients with very different needs and circumstances. My experience in an assisted living facility was particularly meaningful because I enjoyed spending time with elderly patients and learning how important it is to make people feel heard and valued. In the emergency room, I saw how healthcare professionals must remain calm, attentive, and adaptable in unpredictable situations. My time observing physical therapy also showed me the importance of encouragement and patience, especially when patients are working through difficult or frustrating stages of recovery. My current position at the Wellness Center at Tampa has further developed my communication skills. I educate my peers about maintaining their mental health, which has taught me how to approach sensitive topics with compassion and without judgment. It has also reinforced how important it is to listen to people and understand that everyone may need a different kind of support. My involvement in Women in STEM allowed me to work with younger students and encourage their interest in science. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate complex ideas in an engaging and approachable way. Additionally, volunteering at Marklund in Geneva, Illinois, where I assisted individuals with severe disabilities during meals, activities, and sports, taught me the importance of patience, flexibility, and treating every individual with dignity. Together, these experiences have prepared me to enter healthcare with a more complete understanding of what it means to care for others. They have shown me that being a strong healthcare professional means not only applying scientific knowledge, but also building trust, listening carefully, and making every person feel respected and supported.

notes.text:
Throughout high school, I was part of a business academy where I took multiple courses focused on business. As I progressed through the program, I found myself dreading going to class because I could not envision myself pursuing a career in business. I did not want to spend my career behind a desk doing the same thing every day. 

I founded a nonprofit called Baking for the Better, where we fundraise, hold events, and provide outreach to homeless populations. Through the organization, we have worked with two homeless shelters, providing meals for entire shelters as well as donating food, goods, and clothing. My work with Baking for the Better gave me a passion for service and showed me how rewarding it is to provide care and support to people who need it.

This experience led me to explore careers in healthcare. I had always been interested in dentistry, so I began shadowing at a local dental office. Since then, I have shadowed for over 100 hours across several specialties, including orthodontics, pediatrics, periodontics, and general dentistry. These experiences showed me that dentistry combines my interests in working with people, problem-solving, precision, and service.

Through these experiences, I became committed to becoming a dentist. I applied to several early acceptance programs and ultimately chose LECOM. Because LECOM requires me to pursue a science major, I chose Biology at the University of Tampa and plan to matriculate into LECOM’s dental program in 2030.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
My interest in pursuing a career as a physician assistant began through my own experiences with surgery and rehabilitation. During my recovery, I had an amazing orthopedic surgeon and physician assistant whom I still look up to today. Their funny, positive, and bubbly personalities made me feel comfortable and safe during such a hard time in my life. I especially admired my physician assistant because her responsibilities were just as important to my care as my surgeon’s, while she worked alongside and supported the surgeon rather than being the primary leader. I realized this type of role fits my personality because I would rather work as part of a team and support a physician than be the person in charge. I also love that physician assistants can work in different areas of healthcare and have the flexibility to change specialties throughout their careers. I find this exciting because I want a career where I can continue learning and exploring different fields.

I have always been an empathetic and caring person, so I knew I wanted a career focused on helping others. My experiences as a patient showed me how much compassion and genuine care from a healthcare provider can impact someone's recovery. I hope to provide that same comfort and support to my future patients, especially children. I chose Allied Health because it allows me to explore both the physician assistant and physical therapy paths, which are two healthcare fields that interest me.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
I think my job as a lifeguard for the past three summers has been one of the biggest experiences that has prepared me for a career in healthcare. I had to become CPR and First Aid certified, and although I was fortunate that I did not have to make saves often, the one time I did gave me a real understanding of the emergency aspect of healthcare. Realizing that someone’s life is in your hands is a crazy thing to experience, and you do not truly understand the pressure until you are actually in an emergency situation. I am really grateful that lifeguarding gave me that experience.

My volunteer experiences, whether it was coaching children with special needs or spending time socializing with the elderly to keep them company, have also made me much more empathetic. I believe empathy is one of the most important qualities in healthcare. You cannot go into healthcare only for the money or benefits, you have to genuinely care about your patients, and I think that's something that will come naturally to me.

Lastly, my participation in sports throughout my life has played a major role in preparing me for healthcare because it is what sparked my interest in the field in the first place. Through my many sports-related injuries, I have visited athletic trainers, hospitals, orthopedic offices, and physical therapy offices countless times. My own physician assistant also took the time to explain the degrees and programs she went through and what her lifestyle was like as a PA. Hearing about her journey helped me better understand the responsibility that comes with this career and how important academics are to reaching my goals. It made me realize that I need to take my academics more seriously and step up my effort to prepare myself for the future. These experiences have given me a general understanding of different healthcare positions and helped me learn what I would and would not want in a future career.
